title: Frame rotation and geodetic conversion
summary: The two transformations between the representations of a position: the Cartesian rotation about the pole, and the ellipsoidal conversion.

nodes.label: Earth Rotation Angle from UT1
nodes.summary: A linear function of the days of UT1 since J2000.0, in turns.

nodes.label: Eci
nodes.summary: A Cartesian position in the inertial frame, in meters.

nodes.label: Ecef
nodes.summary: A Cartesian position in the Earth-fixed frame, in meters.

nodes.label: Build the rotation matrix
nodes.summary: A clockwise turn about the third axis, whose transpose is the inverse.

nodes.label: Rotate inertial to Earth-fixed
nodes.summary: Apply the rotation to the vector. The length is preserved.

nodes.label: Rotate Earth-fixed to inertial
nodes.summary: Apply the transposed rotation. The length is preserved.

nodes.label: Cartesian to geodetic
nodes.summary: Solve for latitude, longitude, and height on an ellipsoid. Iterative, because no elementary closed form exists.

nodes.label: On the rotation axis?
nodes.summary: No longitude is defined on the axis.

nodes.label: No longitude
nodes.summary: The conversion returns no value rather than an arbitrary longitude.

nodes.label: Geodetic
nodes.summary: Latitude and longitude in radians, height in meters above the WGS 84 ellipsoid.

nodes.label: Geodetic to Cartesian
nodes.summary: Closed form, using the prime vertical radius of curvature.

nodes.label: Geodetic to Ecef
nodes.summary: The Earth-fixed Cartesian position on the WGS 84 ellipsoid.
